identity.title: Position: Principles of Animal Cognition to Improve LLM Evaluations

problem.claim: Understanding and evaluating LLM capabilities is increasingly difficult as models display a wider range of behaviors.

gap.claim: The paper identifies a need for richer evaluation guidance for probing complex intelligent systems, drawing on experimental paradigms and design practices from animal cognition.

contributions.claim: Argues that LLM researchers should apply lessons from animal cognition to evaluation design.
Presents five core evaluation principles derived from animal cognition research and explains their relevance to understanding LLM capabilities and behavior.
Uses an empirical case study to illustrate how the principles can yield a richer picture of transitive inference as a reasoning capability.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by importing animal-cognition experimental paradigms and design practices into LLM evaluation, organized as five core principles.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their principles provide a richer picture of LLM transitive inference in an empirical case study.

narrative_sequence.summary: Broader LLM behavior makes capability understanding and evaluation more challenging.
The paper argues for drawing on animal cognition, a field with established paradigms for probing complex intelligent systems.
It presents five core evaluation principles and explains their proposed guidance for LLM evaluation.
An empirical case study applies the principles to transitive inference and is reported to produce a richer capability picture.

source_observation.claim: The paper connects a general evaluation framework to a concrete case study of transitive inference.

lessons.interpretation: A framework becomes more actionable when its abstract principles are mapped onto one specific capability.
lessons.application: When introducing evaluation principles, pair them with a focused capability-level case study showing what additional behavioral distinctions they expose.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when the target capability lacks a meaningful operational task or when a single case cannot represent the framework's intended scope.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five principles, the case-study design, the reported measurements, or what becomes richer about the transitive-inference evaluation.
No comparison condition or quantitative result is provided, so the extent of the reported improvement cannot be assessed from the abstract alone.
